Patient demographics:
  age: 58
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: North American
  relationship_status: In a relationship
  occupation: Dentist
  trauma_type: Police violence
  pcl5: 77

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid All Feelings: avoid anything that could cause negative or positive feelings, Avoid Stressors: avoid anything that could be stressful, Checking Surroundings: constantly scan environment for signs of threat
  Threat: Threat from Strangers: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations, Sleep Problems: Trouble falling or staying asleep, Safe Seat Seeking: I always choose where to sit based on how safe or protected I feel
  Memory: Memory Feels Alien: The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me, Auditory Recall: When I have memories of what happened I sometimes hear things in my head that I heard during the frightening event., Pain Recall: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
  Negative Appraisals: Intrinsic Fault: There is something about me that made the event happen, Life Destroyed: My life has been destroyed by the trauma, Injustice: What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it

Vignette:
Dr. Hernandez's eyes scanned the crowded coffee shop before he took a seat in the corner, back against the wall. It was a habit he'd developed over the past year, ever since the incident with the police officer. He couldn't shake the feeling of being constantly on guard, as if every stranger who walked by posed a potential threat. Even in ordinary situations, like waiting for his morning coffee, Dr. Hernandez found himself instinctively scanning his surroundings for signs of danger. It had been 14 months since the traumatic event that changed everything for him. He was driving home from a late-night dental emergency when he was pulled over by an officer who claimed his tail light was out. The situation escalated quickly, with the officer becoming increasingly aggressive and eventually using physical force to subdue Dr. Hernandez. He remembered the sound of shattering glass, the feeling of his arm being twisted behind his back, and the searing pain in his shoulder as he hit the pavement. The memory still felt like it belonged to someone else, a detached observer watching a scene unfold from afar. But when it surfaced, as it often did in the dead of night or during quiet moments like this, Dr. Hernandez was transported back to that chaotic scene. He'd hear the officer's angry voice, the screech of tires, and the crunch of breaking glass. His shoulder would throb with a familiar ache, as if the pain had been lying dormant, waiting to be reactivated. Dr. Hernandez had always prided himself on being a rational man, but since the incident, he'd become increasingly convinced that there was something inherently flawed about him that had led to this event. If only he'd driven more carefully, or cooperated more fully with the officer... Maybe then things wouldn't have spiralled out of control. The guilt and self-doubt had become a constant companion, eroding his confidence as a dentist and a partner. His relationship with his girlfriend, Maria, had suffered too. Dr. Hernandez found himself withdrawing from social engagements and intimacy, fearful that any strong emotions might trigger another flashback or episode of anxiety. He'd started to feel like he was living in a state of suspended animation, avoiding anything that could cause negative or positive feelings – essentially, life itself. Maria had been patient and supportive, but Dr. Hernandez knew she couldn't understand why he felt so destroyed by this event. To her, it seemed like an isolated incident, something that should have been resolved with a lawsuit or therapy. But for Dr. Hernandez, the injustice of what happened still burned bright – the sense that he'd been targeted arbitrarily, and that nothing had been done to hold anyone accountable. Sleep had become a luxury Dr. Hernandez could no longer afford. He lay awake most nights, his mind racing with worst-case scenarios and hypothetical threats. Even when exhaustion finally claimed him, he'd wake up after only a few hours, his body tense and alert, ready to respond to some nonexistent danger. As the coffee shop bustled around him, Dr. Hernandez felt the familiar weight of anxiety settle in. He knew it was time to seek help – not just for himself, but for Maria and their relationship. The thought of facing the past head-on terrified him, but he couldn't keep living like this – constantly on edge, avoiding life, and wondering what could have been done differently. With a heavy sigh, Dr. Hernandez stood up, his eyes scanning the room one last time before he walked out into the unknown.
